subject: Growth lift pricing exchange for upcoming term
messages:
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueharbor.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Subject: Revisit pricing ahead of upcoming term (Q2)

Hi Rafael —

Hope you had a good weekend. Quick heads-up from our side: our usage has grown ahead of the forecast and procurement asked us to re-open pricing for the contract renewal coming up in May. Attached is a short usage summary for Q1 (see BlueHarbor_Q1_usage_summary.pdf).

High-level asks from procurement & finance:
- Can Redwood offer a short-term price hold while our legal reviews the amendment?
- We’re evaluating a modest committed uplift for predictable latency-sensitive workloads — what level of unit discount could you provide in exchange for a 20% uplift this year?
- We’d prefer a short true-up window rather than multi-quarter reconciliations.

Would love to set a 30-min sync this week to go over options. I’ve looped Michael (technical lead) and copied Neha from your team.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Partnerships
Blue Harbor Labs
Attachment: BlueHarbor_Q1_usage_summary.pdf
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueharbor.com>; Michael Tran <michael.tran@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Subject: Growth Lift — pricing exchange proposal and next steps

Elena, Michael —

Thanks for the note and for the Q1 summary. Congratulations on the usage lift — great to see the product traction. I put together a short proposal (attached) that I think addresses the three items you flagged. High level: a Growth Lift Exchange that balances predictability for you and unit economics for Redwood. Key points: 

- Commit uplift: 20% uplift in committed monthly capacity over the current baseline for a 12-month amendment.
- Tiered discount: 6% off list for the uplifted capacity band, stepping to 9% if you reach +35% actuals for two consecutive months.
- 45-day true-up after quarter close (we typically support 30–60 day windows; Ben suggests 45 days to align billing and usage reports).
- Price hold: We can offer a 14-day price hold on the amended rates while legal reviews the amendment; after signature rates would be locked for the 12-month term.
- One-time onboarding credit: equivalent to one month of uplifted spend (applied as a credit over the first invoice) in exchange for a 12-month commit.

If that sounds reasonable we should:
1) Take a 30-min call to confirm the uplift baseline and the true-up mechanics (calendar invite attached).
2) I’ll prep an amendment (redline-friendly) and a DocuSign link once procurement confirms they want to proceed with the 14-day hold.

Attached: GrowthLift_Proposal_v1.pdf

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -0700
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>; Elena Soto <elena.soto@blueharbor.com>; Michael Tran <michael.tran@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Subject: RE: Growth Lift — pricing exchange proposal and next steps

Quick follow from the infra/CS side — thanks Rafael for drafting. A couple pragmatic notes based on their Q1 pattern: 

- Burst allowance: we can codify a 10% monthly burst buffer above the committed band for latency-critical requests without immediate overage charges; overages beyond the buffer would be charged at standard list unless true-up bumps the committed band.
- True-up window: Rafael’s proposal for 45 days is fine operationally; it gives us time to reconcile logs with their billing exports.
- Capacity ramp plan: recommend we include a two-month stagger for the initial uplift to avoid sudden scaling events on their infra.

I attached a short playbook excerpt that we can share with Blue Harbor to show how the burst and ramp work (Capacity_Playbook.pdf). If procurement wants a firmer SLA on burst behavior we can add language to the amendment.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Capacity_Playbook.pdf

Subject: Re: Growth Lift — pricing exchange proposal and next steps

Rafael —

Thanks, this is helpful and gets us most of the way there. Procurement asked for two small changes before they’ll approve moving the amendment to legal: 

1) Can the price-hold window be extended to 21 days (procurement needs a little extra review time)?
2) They prefer that the onboarding credit be applied as an up-front credit on the first invoice rather than spread over the first billing cycle.

If Redwood is comfortable with those two tweaks we’ll move this to legal and sign quickly — I’ll also request a DocuSign link. Can you confirm by end of day tomorrow?

Appreciate the fast turnaround — excited to keep scaling with Redwood.

Best,
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Partnerships
Blue Harbor Labs
